items.stem: Why capture a span for each agent step rather than only the final answer?

options.text: Step-level traces show where behaviour went wrong, which a final answer cannot
options.rationale: Correct: per-step visibility is what makes failures diagnosable.

options.text: It makes the answer more creative
options.rationale: Tracing does not change answer content.

options.text: It reduces the model's token cost
options.rationale: Tracing does not lower token usage.

options.text: It is required to send the first request
options.rationale: An agent can run without tracing; tracing is for observability.

items.explanation: Correct: per-step visibility is what makes failures diagnosable.

items.stem: Which TWO practices keep observability safe and usable? (Select TWO.)

options.text: Redact secrets and personal data before writing traces
options.rationale: Correct: redaction keeps sensitive data out of the trace store.

options.text: Sample traces under heavy load to control volume and cost
options.rationale: Correct: sampling keeps observability affordable at scale.

options.text: Write API keys verbatim into every span
options.rationale: Logging secrets is a serious leak.
Turning off tracing removes the observability you need most in production.

items.explanation: Correct: redaction keeps sensitive data out of the trace store.

items.stem: A rare agent failure is hard to reproduce. What capability helps most?

options.text: Replaying the recorded run and diffing it against a successful one
options.rationale: Correct: replay plus diff reproduces the failure and isolates where it diverged.
Guessing the inputs will not faithfully reproduce the failure.
A bigger model does not reproduce a past run.
Removing records destroys the data needed to diagnose.

items.explanation: Correct: replay plus diff reproduces the failure and isolates where it diverged.
